What the numbers show:
- The year-over-year trend is up about 2.1 to 2.7 times (Sep-Oct 2025 vs 2026: 81 to 221; Oct alone: 51 to 138).
- There is a December dip. Last year December was about 42% below November (67 to 39), probably from holidays. The pattern is weaker after a NeurIPS-season peak.
- There were peaks in May (likely the NeurIPS deadline) and October (likely the ICLR deadline and the arXiv flood that follows it). The October 2026 spike may be partly a one-off.
- If Nov-Dec 2026 matches Nov-Dec 2025 scaled by 2.1 to 2.7 times, it lands at about 220 to 290. A flat rate equal to the Jul-Sep average (about 74 a month) gives about 150. Continuing the October rate (138 a month) gives about 275 minus a December dip.
- Older windows may shift slightly as new versions get indexed, so they are not perfectly comparable.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Conference timing: NeurIPS 2026 is in early December, and camera-ready versions get posted to arXiv. ICLR 2027 rebuttals in November may lead to revised versions, and revisions count under the version-date quirk. ICML 2027 submissions are due around late January, so papers for it mostly appear after the window.
- Holiday slowdown: expect fewer submissions from late December through January 1.
- arXiv infrastructure: the cloud migration could cause indexing gaps or backlogs around the window.
- Terminology: substitutes such as "agentic RL" without the full phrase are not counted by the exact-phrase search, so some related papers will be missed.
